posts.title: Reconditioned or used? What the auction sheet really tells you
posts.excerpt: How to read a Japanese auction sheet, which grades to trust, and why a used car's service book matters just as much.

body.text: Reconditioned cars are pre-owned imports, mostly from Japan, that have not yet been registered in Sri Lanka. Used cars are already registered here. Each has its own paper trail, and that trail is the best protection you have against a rolled-back odometer.

body.heading: Reading the grade
body.text: The overall grade runs from 1 to 6, with S for nearly new. Most good imports sit at 4 or 4.5. The interior grade (A to E) tells you how the cabin has been treated. A 4.5/B car is usually a better buy than a 5/C one.

body.heading: The map of the body
body.text: The small car diagram shows every mark the inspector found. A1 is a tiny scratch, U2 a dent the size of a coin, W1 a repair wave that is hard to see. A few A1s are normal. Several W marks on one side deserve a question.

body.heading: Mileage
body.text: The auction sheet records the odometer reading on the day of sale. We print that number on every listing and next to our own reading at handover, so you can see they match.

body.heading: For used cars
body.text: Ask for the service book and agent invoices. Mileage should rise steadily from one stamp to the next. If a car has done 15,000 km a year for five years and then 2,000 km for three, ask why.

posts.title: Leasing in 2026: the Central Bank's new limits, explained
posts.excerpt: Since 25 May 2026 lenders can finance only 40% of an unregistered car. Here is what that means for your down payment.

body.text: On 25 May 2026 the Central Bank of Sri Lanka lowered the maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratios for motor vehicle loans and leases. Every bank, finance company and leasing company has to follow them.

body.heading: The limits
body.text: For cars, SUVs and vans that are unregistered or registered for less than a year, the lender can finance up to 40% of the value, so you put down at least 60%. Commercial vehicles in the same situation can be financed up to 60%. Any vehicle registered and used for more than a year can be financed up to 60%.

body.heading: Flat rate vs reducing balance
body.text: Many leasing offers quote a flat rate, charged on the original amount for the whole term. The reducing-balance rate shows the true cost, because interest is charged only on what you still owe. Our calculator shows both, so you can compare offers fairly.

body.heading: What we do
body.text: We work with several lenders and send your application to the ones most likely to approve it. Figures on this site are estimates; the lender confirms the final rate.

posts.title: Is an EV right for Sri Lankan roads?
posts.excerpt: Charging at home, range in the hill country, battery health checks and the questions we ask every EV buyer.

body.text: Electric cars now lead brand-new car registrations in Sri Lanka. They make the most sense if you can charge at home and mostly drive within a predictable radius.

body.heading: Home charging
body.text: A 7 kW wall box fills most batteries overnight. Before delivery we arrange an electrician to check your supply and earthing.

body.heading: Up-country trips
body.text: Climbing to Nuwara Eliya uses more energy, but you get some back coming down. Plan a top-up on longer trips and you will be fine.

body.heading: Used EVs
body.text: For a used EV the battery state of health matters more than the odometer. We test and print it on every listing.

posts.title: Our 150-point inspection, step by step
posts.excerpt: From paint-depth readings to a hybrid battery test: what happens to every car before it goes on this website.

body.text: Every car we list goes through the same inspection, carried out by our own technicians and signed off by the workshop manager.

body.heading: Body and paint
body.text: We measure paint depth on every panel to find repaints, and check the underbody for flood or accident repairs.

body.heading: Mechanical
body.text: We road-test the car, scan the engine and gearbox for stored faults, check suspension and brakes, and test the hybrid or EV battery.

body.heading: Paperwork
body.text: We match the chassis number to the documents, confirm there is no outstanding finance, and check that the mileage history is consistent.

faqs.q: What is the difference between reconditioned and used?
faqs.a: Reconditioned cars are pre-owned imports, mostly from Japan, that have not yet been registered in Sri Lanka. Used cars are already registered here and have local owners on record.

faqs.q: How much down payment do I need for leasing?
faqs.a: Since 25 May 2026, lenders can finance up to 40% of an unregistered or newly registered car, so you need at least 60% down. For cars registered and used over a year, and for commercial vehicles, they can finance up to 60%. Our calculator applies these rules automatically.

faqs.q: Can I see the auction sheet before visiting?
faqs.a: Yes. Every reconditioned car has its auction sheet and an English translation on the listing, and we can send the original on WhatsApp.
Yes. Send us your car's details and a few photos through the Sell or trade-in page and we will reply with a price range, usually the same day.
We deliver island-wide. Delivery within 30 km of Nugegoda is free; further away we charge the driver's cost only.

faqs.q: Is the price on the website the final price?
faqs.a: The listed price includes all duties and our fees. Registration (for reconditioned and brand-new cars) and insurance are extra and we tell you the exact amount up front.

faqs.q: Do your cars come with a warranty?
faqs.a: Brand-new cars carry the agent warranty. Reconditioned and used cars come with our 6-month engine and gearbox cover, and you can extend it.

faqs.q: How do I reserve a car?
faqs.a: Pay a refundable deposit of Rs 100,000 and we hold the car for 5 days while your finance is approved.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own mechanic?
faqs.a: Of course. Book a viewing and bring whoever you trust. We will put the car on a lift for them.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to buy?
faqs.a: Your NIC or passport and proof of address. For leasing, the lender will also ask for proof of income.

chat.fallback: I'm a simple demo assistant, so I might have missed that. Try a budget or car type, or ask about leasing, trade-ins or delivery.

leasing.text: Since 25 May 2026, lenders can finance up to 40% of an unregistered or newly registered car, so you need at least 60% down. Cars registered over a year and commercial vehicles can be financed up to 60%. The leasing calculator works it out for you.

tradeIn.text: Yes, we take trade-ins. Send a few photos and details and we usually reply with a price range the same day.

history.text: Every reconditioned car has its auction sheet and English translation on the listing, and we print the verified mileage. For used cars we show the service history.

delivery.text: We deliver island-wide. Within 30 km of Nugegoda it's free; further away we only charge the driver's cost.

warranty.text: Brand-new cars carry the agent warranty. Reconditioned and used cars come with our 6-month engine and gearbox cover.

location.text: We're at 214 High Level Road, Nugegoda. Open Mon–Sat 9.00–18.00 and Sun 10.00–14.00.

reserve.text: A refundable Rs 100,000 deposit holds a car for 5 days while your finance is approved.

testDrive.text: Happy to arrange that. Pick a car and a time slot and we'll confirm on WhatsApp.
